subject: Fuaran-Core
$comment: This repository's claims ladder, declared as data. It is `proofs/README.md`'s own ladder — what is PROVED, what is only TESTED, what is ASSUMED — in a schema a tool can read, so the question does not have to be answered by reading prose and hoping two documents use the same words. A `not claimed` item is the ABSENCE of a row, never a row: the README enumerates those, and enumerating them here would turn a disclaimer into a claim. Levels are the closed set proved | tested | assumed | policy. Authored by hand, never generated — editing the ladder means editing this file and the README together.

claims.claim: On the model, for every N and every permutation of a lane set, the fold halts with the same canonical conflict report or folds to the same state. Proved with no assume and no admit under --report_assumes error; the fold half under `independence_diamond` for a lane set whose lanes all apply from the base, the halt half under no hypothesis at all.
Every decode combinator reaches exactly one outcome on every input, and which one is characterised structurally — so the failure classification is exhaustive rather than merely non-empty.

The recursive node decoder is total on an arbitrary JSON value and succeeds on exactly the well-formed documents. Termination is content here rather than a formality: the decoder descends into a child array obtained by name, so nothing structural is visible at the call site.
Decoding an encoded node returns that node, for every node of the reference vocabulary, at every depth.

On every document the read policy does not name, the tolerant and strict readers accept the same values and refuse the same documents — a promise about the VERDICT, not about the message; on a document with no null at all the two are literally the same function.

Production's delta recovery from a content-addressed DAG, its pairwise conflict sweep, the composition and the replay together agree with the extracted model over three lane pools, per lane set and per sampled arrival order — outcome and composed merge script, not merely a hash. Agreement is over the sets drawn and the orders enumerated, never over all inputs.

The extracted decode model agrees with the shipped combinators over the wire corpus and a generated sample, compared on outcome CLASS, decoded VALUE and error MESSAGE at once — a model agreeing on accept-versus-refuse alone would not notice a decoder naming the wrong expectation. A blind bridge reading every integer as a float is required to make the comparison fail, so a green report is known to be one that can lose.

The fold theorem's one domain hypothesis: two operations whose footprints are declared disjoint, and which both apply at a state, each apply after the other and reach the same state. Sampled — never proved — including directly against the extracted model's own independence predicate on the reference witness, with a sample-adequacy guard and its own go-red. This row is about a DOMAIN'S OWN witness, which is what the fold theorem is generic over; for the skeleton-op tree algebra specifically it is no longer assumed but proved, at `tree-independence-diamond` below.

evidence.assumption: independence_diamond holds of the domain the fold is run over

claims.claim: The fold half is stated for a lane set whose every lane applies cleanly from the base state. Nothing is proved about a lane set one of whose lanes rejects; the halt half still covers it whenever it halts.

evidence.assumption: lanes_apply — every lane of the set applies from the base state

claims.claim: What of the DAG layer remains outside the model, narrowed by Phase 134 from 'all of it'. `Dag.mergeBase` is outside this path entirely — `foldOnce` hands `reconcileMany` the base node's id directly and no divergence point is ever located — so nothing is claimed about it at any level. Hashing is abstracted behind an opaque minting function; what it buys is stated separately as `node-ids-distinct`. The ancestor closure, the difference against the base's closure, the lookup and the fold built on them are no longer assumed: see `dag-delta-recovery` and `fold-from-the-dag`.

evidence.assumption: Dag.mergeBase, and the hash function itself, are correct

claims.claim: The proof leg holds the committed oracle to a fresh extraction byte for byte, which makes 'the oracle is the model' a checked claim; it does not make the F# backend correct. The least-examined link in the chain, and named as such.

evidence.assumption: the F* extractor and the F# compiler are correct

claims.claim: The model reads sets as lists under membership and the host compares canonical (deduplicated, sorted) reports, so multiplicity and order inside a report are unobserved by construction.

evidence.assumption: the list-for-set reading loses nothing the comparison observes

claims.claim: That the parser's absorption of object-member nulls is equivalent to erasing member nulls from the document tree the strict grammar would otherwise produce. The near-miss tokens that make this an assumption rather than a theorem are grammar, and stay with the parser; the differential is the evidence for it, not a proof of it.

evidence.assumption: the parser's member-null fork equals erasing member nulls from the strict tree

claims.claim: Which prover is pinned, how many cold-cache runs a check is, and that a model edited without re-extracting fails the leg — the reproducibility posture the proved rows above are only as good as. Policy, not algebra: no theorem addresses it.

For the base-plus-N-chains shape — one shared base node and one linear chain per writer, which is what the fold's own generator builds and what a local-first deployment has — the delta of a lane off the base is that lane's nodes, and its ops, in append order. The whole layer computed rather than assumed: the head's ancestor closure, the base's, the topological order, the difference and the lookup. Under the id-distinctness premise, and with the CHOICE of topological order named separately as an assumption.

The fold over the DAG is the fold over the lane lists, and the confluence law therefore holds stated from the content-addressed DAG rather than from deltas someone had already recovered: the same heads over the same base fold to the same state, or halt with the same canonical report, however the heads arrive.

Production's own ancestor closure, topological order and delta recovery, on the DAG the fold's generator actually builds, agree per lane with the extracted model's recovery over the SAME nodes across three lane pools — the ids the model walks are the content hashes production minted, so a disagreement can only be about the recovery and never about the hash. A DAG whose lanes hang off the wrong parent is required to make the comparison fail, and two vacuity guards refuse a run that recovered no ops or walked no chain longer than one node.

The hash-collision assumption, and since Phase 134 the only thing the delta recovery assumes about content addressing. Node ids are distinct, so the node a chain named is the node the DAG returns for it; two nodes sharing a content id is the only way that fails.

evidence.assumption: Dag.nodeHash is injective on (sorted parents, actor, encoded op)

claims.claim: That the order production picks and the order the model computes are the same order. Production drains a ready frontier smallest-id-first; the model reverses the parent walk. On a spine every pair of the closure is comparable, so exactly one topological order exists and the two must coincide — argued, and measured by the differential against the real recovery, but not mechanised. Everything downstream of the order is proved.

evidence.assumption: a spine admits exactly one topological order, and the frontier drain produces it

claims.claim: For the skeleton-op tree algebra, two operations whose footprints are declared disjoint and which both apply at an id-unique tree each apply after the other and reach the same tree — the fold theorem's domain hypothesis, proved rather than sampled, for twelve of the fifteen unordered operation pairs (the three left open are one shape, at `tree-algebra-batch-nesting`). Nine of the twelve are closed by the conservative footprint alone and never look at a tree: a remove or a move writes an unknown parent, independence refuses that against any structural write, and every skeleton operation except a do-nothing batch writes structure — so such a pair is independent only where the other operation does nothing at all.

Fold confluence for the skeleton-op tree algebra with NO domain hypothesis remaining, over the non-batch operation alphabet: the same lanes reach the same tree however they arrive, a lane set that cannot fold halts with the same canonical report however it arrives, and none folds under one order and halts under another. The halt half is proved separately under no hypothesis at all — not the diamond, not id uniqueness, nothing about the apply engine.

The unconditional statement 'every accepted skeleton operation preserves id uniqueness' is FALSE of the algebra as it stands, and this is a machine-checked counterexample rather than an assertion: the insert validation tests the inserted node's OWN id against the tree and not its descendants, so a concrete accepted insert leaves the tree carrying an id twice. Proved beside it: the conditional form — an insert whose subtree is internally id-unique and disjoint from the tree preserves the invariant — and its converse, so 'the result is id-unique' and 'the insert was fresh' are the same statement. That pair is the specification the fix has to meet.

The extracted tree model agrees with the shipped apply engine and footprint derivation over the generated operation pool and every state a prefix of it reaches — the footprint as four address sets, the verdict, an accepted result through the content hash computed by production's own function on both sides, and a rejection by class. Every rejection class the plain apply can raise is asserted reached BY NAME rather than counted, and a bridge that erases every kind tag is required to make the result comparison fail, so a green report is known to be one that can lose.

The tree the algebra runs over carries each id at most once. This is a hypothesis rather than an oversight: the lookup that resolves an id returns the FIRST match in document order, so on a tree carrying one id twice what it returns is a fact about the order as well as the contents — and a reorder moves the order, which makes the diamond FALSE there rather than merely unproved. Nothing in the estate produces such a tree and the structural diff refuses one outright, but no shipped type carries the invariant.

evidence.assumption: the tree the fold runs over carries each id at most once

claims.claim: The proved diamond covers twelve of the fifteen operation pairs; the three left open are one shape — either side a batch that neither does nothing nor relocates. A batch is a list of operations written as one operation and the fold already threads a list, so excluding it removes no behaviour: it declines to nest one lane inside another. Lifting the leaf diamond along a batch script is the argument the fold theorem already performs at lane granularity, and it needs the id-uniqueness invariant at each intermediate state of the script, which is what `insert-breaks-id-uniqueness` currently denies.

evidence.assumption: an operation pair in which either side is a non-trivial nested batch

claims.claim: A content-addressed DAG grown from nothing by append and merge alone, each naming parents the DAG already held, has no integrity break; and a linear hash chain grown from genesis by append alone verifies. The id half is free by construction, but the parent half is not: append does not check that the parent it is handed names a node the DAG holds, so every-parent-present is a precondition on how a DAG was grown rather than a property of the constructor, and the theorem carries it as one.

Changing one DAG node's op, actor or parent multiset while leaving its address as it was, in a DAG whose node under that id was intact, is reported as a break; and the same for one linear record's sequence, actor or op with its two hash fields left alone. Both are corollaries of a characterisation of the walker itself: the walk finds nothing exactly when every key is its content hash and every named parent is present, and exactly when every record's sequence, prev-link and recomputed hash agree.

Three break classes are proved under NO hypothesis at all, which is the sharpest thing the mechanisation says: a linear record renumbered, a linear record re-pointed at a different predecessor, and a DAG node another node names being absent. Those three checks compare stored data against the walk's own running values or against the key set, and never consult the hash — so they are detectable independently of the hash's strength. Only the recomputed-hash check spends the cryptographic premise.

merge(A,B) and merge(B,A) converge to one content id, because the parents are sorted before hashing. Needs only that the comparison is a total order and nothing about the hash. Its converse is proved too and is a boundary rather than a result: re-ordering a node's parents is NOT a detectable tamper, and is not meant to be.

The extracted model agrees with Dag.firstBreak and OpStream.firstChainBreak over generated DAGs and chains and every single-node tamper of each, comparing the verdict, the location, WHICH check failed and the expected and got values at once — and mints production's own content ids node by node, which is checkable only through append because nodeHash is private. Two go-red cases require a model handed a different hash to disagree, and a third runs one tamper under two hashes: found under the real one, INVISIBLE under a deliberately non-injective one, to production and to the model alike. Every run asserts that detection actually happened, because two walkers that both say intact agree perfectly and certify nothing.

The one cryptographic premise, and the whole of what tamper detection rests on: two contents that hash to one id are the same content. It is an explicit lemma-valued PARAMETER of the theorems that need it rather than an assume, so which results depend on it is visible in their signatures. It is stated MODULO THE PARENT SORT, which is the strongest true form. And it bundles three things the model does not decompose: the hash injective on the pre-images that occur, the two splices in the pre-image unambiguous (no comma inside a parent id, no second place the pipe could split the actor encoding from the op encoding), and the op codec injective.

evidence.assumption: Dag.nodeHash and the chain payload hash are injective on the pre-images that occur

claims.claim: That the order the model walks is the order production walks. Production enumerates Map.toList, which is ascending key order; the model walks the list it is given, and the differential hands it exactly that list. The VERDICT is order-independent by construction — a break exists or it does not — so only which break is reported first depends on this, and nothing here is said about F#'s Map enumeration.

evidence.assumption: the entry list the model is handed is Map.toList's own order

claims.claim: The recursive-descent JSON parser reaches exactly one outcome on every input — an accepted value or a CLASSIFIED refusal, never both and never neither. That it is Tot at all is the content rather than a formality: F* admits the mutual group only after showing it terminates on every input, and a recursive-descent parser over a mutable index has no syntactic reason to. Every consuming sub-parser carries the remaining input's strict decrease in its RETURN TYPE, and that refinement is the whole termination argument.

On the canonical nesting family the depth bound is EXACT at every depth and for every suffix: the parse succeeds iff the cap is at least the nesting, and refuses by name when it is not. Stated this way because the obvious form is false — the parser is left to right and the first failure wins, so a document that is both too deep and malformed earlier fails with the earlier kind. The other two halves are depth_error_only_at_a_container (the kind is confined to a container position, carried in every signature's return type so it is re-checked at every call site) and depth_bound_scalars_unaffected (a scalar parses at a cap of zero, where every container is refused).

Every integer token the parser ACCEPTS denotes an int53-safe value, whichever branch produced it — JInt by the Int32 range, JFloat by the guard. Note where the guard is NOT: the Int32 branch runs no int53 test and needs none, because the Int32 range is a strict subset (int32_within_int53 proves it).

The int53 guard as production spells it — a lexical comparison against the range's own digits — never admits an integer whose VALUE is outside the range. This is the half that matters: over-refusing costs a user an error message, under-refusing costs a corrupted identifier.

The int53 guard is NOT exact, and cannot be as written: Wire.fs justifies its lexical comparison with 'JSON forbids leading zeros', which this parser's digit loop does not enforce, so 0009007199254740992 — exactly 2^53, the largest int53-safe integer there is — is refused as MalformedNumber because its STRING is 19 characters. Proved as a witness rather than described, so that anyone who 'fixes' the guard to match its own comment reddens a lemma and is told the parser's behaviour changed. The error only ever runs this way; soundness above is the other half.

Every one of the twelve JsonErrorKind cases is REACHABLE, by a named witness input — a classification whose cases are unreachable is closed but not exhaustive, and the difference is what makes the differential's coverage mean anything. The confinement half is carried in the parsers' return types rather than asserted once, so it is re-checked at every call site: parse_string cannot report a number failure, the descent cannot report TrailingCharacters (which the entry point constructs from the leftover-input test rather than raising), and MaxDepthExceeded cannot arise anywhere but at a container.

The extracted model agrees with Json.parseDetailedWithPolicy over a 55-input near-miss table under both read policies, every wire-corpus nodes/ and ops/ fixture as raw text, both nesting families at every depth 0-8 under every cap 0-8, arrays and objects up to 64 members, and 4,000 seed-replayable generated inputs — comparing the outcome class, the decoded value, and on a failure the KIND, the POSITION and the MESSAGE at once. Two go-red cases: a model holding a cap production has already spent must accept what production refuses by name, and a blind bridge hiding the two container characters must break every structured document while leaving a scalar in agreement. The member-null fork is asserted to have FIRED, because two parsers that never met a member null agree about a policy neither exercised.

System.Double.TryParse's three-valued verdict on a number token — parses finitely, parses to a non-finite, does not parse — is a PARAMETER of the model, instantiated by the differential host with the call production makes. What the model decides is which verdict leads where, which is the parser's own logic; nothing here is said about float precision, about which tokens .NET accepts, or about the shortest-round-trip layout. System.Int32.TryParse is likewise modelled lexically, as a comparison against the range's own digits after stripping leading zeros, which is argued rather than mechanised and measured by the differential's boundary cases from both sides.

evidence.assumption: the float readback and the Int32 range test are the host's, not the model's

claims.claim: That the model's character list IS the production string. A character is a constructor of the model's alphabet — one per character the parser distinguishes, plus a catch-all carrying the character verbatim, so two different characters are never identified — and the host's one-line-per-character bridge is what makes the correspondence. The bridge is not itself proved. The value of a \uXXXX escape is on the same footing: the model carries the four hex digits symbolically because the extraction carries no integers, and the host resolves the code point, so the decoded character is compared but the transliteration is sampled rather than proved.

evidence.assumption: the host's toCh bridge maps each production character to the model's alphabet faithfully
